If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis
Details:
- What the test does:
  - testPrimitiveTypeClassSerialization iterates over primitive Class objects (byte.class, short.class, int.class, long.class, float.class, double.class, boolean.class, char.class, void.class) and calls SerializationUtils.clone on each, asserting the clone equals the original.

- Execution path:
  - SerializationUtils.clone(T) serializes the input object to a byte array, then deserializes it using a custom ObjectInputStream:
    - serialize(obj, OutputStream) writes the object via a standard ObjectOutputStream (lines 130–139).
    - During deserialization, clone constructs a ClassLoaderAwareObjectInputStream using the original object’s class loader (line 88), then calls in.readObject() (lines 95–96).

- Where it fails:
  - ClassLoaderAwareObjectInputStream overrides resolveClass(ObjectStreamClass) (lines 262–270):
    - It obtains the class name from the stream (desc.getName()) and tries to load it via Class.forName(name, false, classLoader).
    - If that fails, it tries again with the thread context class loader.
    - If both attempts fail, it throws ClassNotFoundException.

- Why primitives fail:
  - When deserializing a Class object representing a primitive type (e.g., int.class), ObjectStreamClass.getName() returns the primitive name like "int".
  - Class.forName("int", ...) always throws ClassNotFoundException because primitive types are not loadable via Class.forName by name.
  - The custom resolveClass method does not fall back to ObjectInputStream’s default resolution (which handles primitive types), nor does it map primitive names to their corresponding Class literals.
  - Consequently, readObject() propagates ClassNotFoundException, which SerializationUtils.clone wraps as a SerializationException with message "ClassNotFoundException while reading cloned object data" (lines 98–101).

- Additional context:
  - For classes loaded by the bootstrap loader (like primitives), object.getClass().getClassLoader() is null; however, even using any loader, Class.forName("int", ...) is invalid.
  - The default ObjectInputStream.resolveClass would correctly handle primitive descriptors, but the custom override bypasses that logic and never calls super.resolveClass(desc).

- Root cause:
  - SerializationUtils.ClassLoaderAwareObjectInputStream.resolveClass(ObjectStreamClass) mishandles primitive types by always delegating to Class.forName and never falling back to the superclass implementation or explicitly mapping primitive names. This causes ClassNotFoundException when cloning Class objects for primitive types (and potentially affects arrays of primitives where special name forms like "[I" may also require careful handling).

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
